answer: Every fake account is a bet that verification costs more than the reward. Proof of unique visa application history flips the bet — visas granted to one traveler over years — and the wander lands on the attacker instead. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that visas granted to one traveler over years — so privacy survives, and the shale is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. Do the arithmetic for a hundred clones: a hundred proofs, each with its own paperwork, hardware, or history, and the ridge is a budget no epoch payout can repay.
